subject: social_science

concepts.title: Sexual Division of Labour and Patriarchy
concepts.definition: A customary arrangement where domestic chores and caregiving are allocated primarily to females, while males undertake income-generating activities outside the household under male-dominated authority structures.
concepts.key_idea: Gender roles are socially constructed rather than biologically determined, rendering unpaid domestic work undervalued.
question_patterns: Explain what is meant by the sexual division of labour.
How does patriarchy influence the allocation of household work?
Why is unpaid domestic labour performed by women often unrecognised?
Describe the distinction between public and private division of labour.
What factors perpetuate male dominance in the domestic sphere?

solution_steps.explain: Household tasks like cooking and caregiving are socially assigned to women within the family.
Men predominantly take up income-producing public jobs, devaluing domestic work despite the longer total hours women work.

concepts.title: Feminist Movements and Gender Inequalities
concepts.definition: Organised collective mobilisations aimed at achieving equal rights, legal status, career access, and social parity for women across public and family life.
concepts.key_idea: Political mobilisation on gender issues improves female literacy, career access, and civic rights.
question_patterns: Define feminism and state its primary objectives.
What are the major indicators of gender inequality in India?
How do feminist movements advocate for personal and family equality?
Examine the causes behind low female literacy and adverse child sex ratio.
Illustrate how the Equal Remuneration Act attempts to address gender wage gaps.

solution_steps.explain: Advocacy for identical rights, legal protections, and life opportunities for both men and women.
Disparities such as female literacy deficits, wage discrimination, and skewed child sex ratios need political intervention.

concepts.title: Women Political Representation and Quotas
concepts.section: Gender and politics - Women's political representation
concepts.definition: The formal inclusion of women in decision-making assemblies ensured through legally mandated reservations in elected political institutions.
concepts.key_idea: Statutory reservations empower disadvantaged groups to shape governance and policy priorities.
question_patterns: Describe the status of women representation in Indian legislatures.
How has local self-government improved female political empowerment?
What provisions are made under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam 2023?
Why is legislative reservation deemed necessary for women?
Compare India female parliamentary representation with international benchmarks.

solution_steps.explain: Historically low representation in Parliament and State Assemblies made affirmative legal mechanisms essential.
Mandating one-third quota in Panchayati Raj institutions and legislative assemblies secures direct participation for women.

concepts.title: Religion and Politics Interface
concepts.definition: The constructive integration of ethical values, moral principles, and social justice demands derived from religious traditions into democratic governance.
concepts.key_idea: Religious values can guide political morality positively when all faiths receive impartial treatment.
question_patterns: Explain Gandhiji view on the relation between religion and politics.
How can moral values drawn from religion enrich democratic politics?
Why do human rights organizations demand protection for minority communities?
Discuss the demand for reform in discriminatory family laws.
Under what conditions does the expression of religious interests remain healthy in politics?

solution_steps.explain: Gandhian philosophy views religion as universal ethics rather than sectarian doctrine.
The state may intervene to protect minority rights and reform unfair personal laws while treating all faiths equally.

concepts.title: Communalism and Forms of Communal Politics
concepts.definition: An exclusionary political ideology founded on the presumption that followers of a single religion constitute an exclusive community with conflicting interests against other faiths.
concepts.key_idea: Communalism polarises society by subordinating shared civil identities to sectarian interests.
question_patterns: What constitutes communal politics?
List the various forms that communalism takes in politics.
How do emotional appeals and religious symbols foster communal polarisation?
Why is the assumption of uniform religious community interests flawed?
Explain how communalism can escalate into violent riots and conflict.

solution_steps.explain: Belief that religion forms the sole foundation of social identity and political loyalty.
Manifests through everyday stereotypes, majoritarian dominance quests, sectarian voting appeals, and physical violence.

concepts.title: Constitutional Provisions of a Secular State
concepts.section: Religion, communalism and politics - Secular state
concepts.definition: A constitutional framework ensuring that the state possesses no official religion, guarantees individual religious freedoms, and prohibits faith-based discrimination.
concepts.key_idea: A secular constitution guarantees religious neutrality and empowers the state to reform internal social inequalities.
question_patterns: Mention the key constitutional provisions that make India a secular state.
How does the Indian Constitution balance religious freedom with state intervention?
Why does India have no official religion unlike some neighbouring countries?
Explain the prohibition of untouchability as a secular reform.
What measures are needed beyond constitutional law to combat communal prejudices?

solution_steps.explain: No single faith receives special constitutional status or official recognition in India.
Citizens enjoy freedom of conscience and propagation, while discrimination is barred and regressive social practices are outlawed.

concepts.title: Caste Inequalities and Social Change
concepts.definition: An institutionalised, hereditary social hierarchy unique to India that historically enforced occupational restrictions, social exclusion, and untouchability.
concepts.key_idea: Urbanisation, educational expansion, and legal bans have eroded traditional caste barriers, though economic disparities persist.
question_patterns: What distinguishing features characterised the traditional caste system in India?
How have urbanisation and occupational mobility altered caste hierarchies?
Describe the contributions of social reformers in challenging caste discrimination.
In what ways do caste-based economic disparities continue in modern India?
Why are certain socio-historical advantages still visible among upper castes?

solution_steps.explain: Hereditary occupations sanctioned by ritual hierarchy and endogamy enforced rigid social stratification.
Economic modernisation and statutory protections weaken segregation, though wealth gaps linked to historical privileges remain.

concepts.title: Forms of Caste in Politics
concepts.section: Caste and politics - Caste in politics
concepts.definition: The strategic alignment where political entities appeal to caste identities, nominate candidates based on caste demographics, and accommodate varied caste interests in governance.
concepts.key_idea: Universal adult suffrage compels politicians to mobilise support across diverse caste communities.
question_patterns: How do political parties utilise caste equations during elections?
Explain the role of caste sentiment in candidate selection and cabinet formation.
What effect did universal adult franchise have on low-caste political consciousness?
Describe how caste groups function as political constituencies.
In what manners do election campaigns appeal to caste identity?

solution_steps.explain: Parties evaluate caste demographics to select viable candidates and build winning electoral alliances.
One-person-one-vote empowers historically marginalised castes to assert democratic influence.

concepts.title: Limitations of Caste Factor in Elections
concepts.section: Caste and politics - Limits of caste in elections
concepts.definition: The electoral reality that caste alignment alone cannot guarantee victory due to cross-cutting economic interests, multi-caste constituencies, and voter evaluation of government performance.
concepts.key_idea: Elections are decided by multiple intersecting factors including governance performance, leadership ratings, and party loyalty rather than pure caste allegiance.
question_patterns: State two reasons why caste alone cannot determine election results in India.
Why is no parliamentary constituency completely dominated by a single caste?
How do economic differences within a single caste affect voting choices?
Why do sitting legislators and ruling parties regularly lose elections despite caste calculations?
Explain why the concept of a monolithic caste vote bank is misleading.

solution_steps.explain: Constituencies have diverse multi-caste demographics requiring cross-community appeals.
Economic divisions within castes and public scrutiny of governance track records drive electoral outcomes.

concepts.title: Politicisation of Caste and its Dual Impact
concepts.section: Caste and politics - Politics in caste
concepts.definition: The reciprocal process through which political engagement alters caste boundaries by fostering coalitions, broader category alignments, and demands for dignity, while risking sectarian conflict.
concepts.key_idea: Politics transforms caste groups into negotiated coalitions that demand power sharing, but excessive caste-centrism can generate social strife.
question_patterns: How does politics influence and reshape caste identities in India?
What is meant by the politicisation of caste?
Discuss the positive outcomes of expressing caste differences in politics.
What are the negative consequences of exclusive caste-based political mobilisation?
How do new caste coalitions like backward and forward groups emerge?

solution_steps.explain: Caste groups expand through sub-caste coalitions and federate into broader social blocs like backward or forward classes.
Provides backward communities leverage for social dignity while risking distraction from broader developmental goals.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Mention constitutional provisions that make India a secular state.

solution_template.explain: The Indian Constitution accords no official status or special privilege to any single faith.
All persons are granted freedom to practice, profess, and propagate their chosen faith, with discrimination on grounds of religion explicitly prohibited.

worked_examples.question_pattern: State two reasons to say that caste alone cannot determine election results in India.

solution_template.explain: No single parliamentary seat in India has an absolute majority of one caste, making broader multi-caste alliances necessary.
Voters from the same caste divide their preferences based on economic class, and sitting representatives frequently lose re-election based on performance.
